title: Aggrega Catalog (Feature)
description: A modular operational feature that binds dynamically to components.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the feature (e.g., 1.0.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

labels.description: Duck-typing labels for the Feature. The reserved label 'feature.aggrega.ai/kind' with value 'secret' marks this as a credential Feature, which routes the attachment through the credential pipeline. A credential Feature and an ordinary Feature are attached the same way, under the same attachment surface; the label selects the pipeline, not the authoring block.

feature.aggrega.ai/kind.description: Feature kind label. Value 'secret' marks this as a credential Feature.

annotations.description: Immutable, intrinsic feature characteristics authored by the Platform Architect in Domain 2. Cascades down to the .context.annotations.catalog bucket.

spec.description: The validation, targeting, and interoperability contract for a catalog Feature: the free-form pillars (values, infra, provides) authored via schema, the fixed-shape pillars (usesSchema dependency sockets, featuresSchema attachment slots), component targeting (appliesTo and appliesToAnyOf), and interoperability controls.

extends.description: URI of a base Feature to inherit YAML metadata from and auto-merge JSON Schema 2020-12 declarations with.

featuresSchema.description: Declarative attachment slot definitions: the named binding points at which this Feature expects a further Feature to be attached. A slot constrains which fill may bind it (selector) and how the fill's material may be delivered (inject); the fill's own Feature owns its values and infra contract. Declaring a slot never closes the attachment block — a deployment may attach a Feature under a name no slot declares. A slot is a binding point, not a dependency socket: usesSchema declares the separate topology surface.

required.description: Declares that the slot must end up bound. On a Component's slot this halts the build when nothing binds the slot's name on an instance of that Component. A Feature's own slots have no surface to be bound from — an attachment declares type, description, values, uses and inject, and carries no nested attachment block — so on a Feature slot this field is a declaration only, read by the Workload cross-check that validates a resource-generating FeatureRecipe's container attachment references against the slots the implemented Feature declares.

inject.description: Allowed inject mechanisms for the slot's material. Empty array = blackbox (the FeatureRecipe controls delivery internally).

description.description: Human documentation for this attachment slot.

sensitive.description: Declares that whatever fills this slot handles secret material. A marker, not a constraint: no fill is accepted or rejected because of it, and no rendered output changes. The declaration is carried onto the slot's generated validation schema, where tooling can read it, and is read when deriving whether the attachment filling this slot handles sensitive material.

selector.description: Optional Kubernetes-style label selector constraining which Feature may fill this slot — the slot analog of a usesSchema socket's selector, evaluated against the attached Feature's own labels. A fill whose labels do not satisfy it halts. Omit to place no constraint on the fill.

appliesTo.description: Kubernetes-style label-selector string matching Components. Comma-separated requirements all must hold (AND). Supported forms: key=value, key!=value, key in (v1, v2), key notin (v1, v2), bare key (label present), !key (label absent). Example: "tier in (critical, production), !legacy". An empty or absent selector declares no constraint. The pattern here is a loose shape gate; the compiler's selector parser performs the full grammar validation.

appliesToAnyOf.description: A list of selectors; the Feature applies if ANY item matches (OR logic). Each item is either a label-selector string (same grammar as appliesTo; requirements inside the string AND together) or a flat key-value map where every pair must match (equality only).

oneOf.description: A label-selector string; same grammar as appliesTo.
A flat map of label key-value pairs; all pairs must match (equality only).

interoperability.description: Advanced operational safety and interoperability controls.

conflictsWith.description: List of feature names that cannot be attached to the same component simultaneously.

componentRefPath.description: String path defining where the compiler should inject the resolved target ID of the component.

usesSchema.description: Native YAML schema defining the topology. The Go CLI natively reads this to validate selectors and allowed inject paradigms.

selector.description: Kubernetes-style selector evaluated natively by the Go compiler in Step 4 to guarantee Cross-Node Type Safety before Wasm execution.

inject.description: Allowlisted delivery contracts (e.g., ['env', 'file']). If omitted, delivery dictation is banned (Black-Box pattern).

schema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 content covering the free-form pillars: values (the Developer's domain — application-shape parameters the Developer configures per Feature attachment in the Aggregate); infra (the Operator's domain — physical sizing knobs supplied by the Release); and provides (downstream context keys this Feature exposes to consumers via the topology pipe). Accepts three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch: (1) inline content (a YAML map carrying compact form, JSON Schema YAML, or mixed); (2) single-file replacement via {$import: <path>}; (3) cross-document reference via {$ref: <Library>#/schemas/<name>} into a SchemaLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). The companion fields usesSchema and featuresSchema cover the fixed-shape pillars (dependency sockets, attachment slots); the bridge synthesis composes the three into the entity's unified validation surface.

assertions.description: Build-time cross-field validation. Each entry is a named assertion: the key is a stable rule identifier surfaced in error messages; the value is a Go template string with `{{ fail "message" }}` halt semantics. Multiple named assertions per entity evaluate per-instance in author-declared order; the first failing assertion halts the build. Feature assertions evaluate at Step 4b (post-resolution, post-analyzer-gate, pre-render) and express architectural invariants of the contract. Template context: .values / .infra / .uses / .features / .metadata. The evaluator uses missingkey=error: references to undefined keys halt with a no-such-key diagnostic. Because the bare reference halts before any fallback can run, a plain `default` does not supply an optional-field fallback on this surface — gate the reference with `hasKey`, or read it through `index` and then apply `default`, or use the `optional` helper, which performs the presence check directly.
